title.narrative: Inception phase University of Rwanda Vaccines incl EU-delegation
Planeringsfas University of Rwanda Vaccin inkl EU-delegering

description.narrative: EU and the Embassy of Sweden have agreed on an inception phase of Rwanda-Sweden MAV Team Europe Initiative. The inception phase is expected to lead to a full contribution with the objective to strengthen capacity for vaccine development and manufacturing in Rwanda, starting in February 2025. In addition, the Embassy of Sweden have agreed on an inception phase of research on vaccine uptake to understand potential bottlenecks in vaccination. We are anticipating a full phase from fall 2025. The funding is jointly undertaken by Sida and the Canadian IDRC to the University of Rwanda in regional collaboration as well as with researchers in Canada and Sweden.

Inception phase of Rwanda-Sweden for a delegated Team Europe Initiative, MAV+, expected to lead to full contribution with the objective to strengthen capacity for vaccine development and manufacturing in Rwanda; and a planning phase of a research program at University of Rwanda for vaccine uptake and accpetance.

Planeringsfas av Rwanda-Sverige för genomförandet av Team Europe Initiative MAV+ som förväntas leda till full insats med målsättningen att stärka kapacitet för vaccinutveckling och produktion i Rwanda, samt planeringsfas med Rwandauniversitetet för att sätta upp ett projekt runt vaccinaccpetans.

The main output from the inception phase of MAV was the full proposal for the full implementation of the MAV program, which was received and assessed and resulted in agreements with the partners (intervention 16785).
Amongst achieved results, the most important ones are:
- A jointly prepared full project proposal, based on benchmarking, workshops, experience sharing, and relationship building. The proposal/project description includes a plan for monitoring, results logframe, indicators, risk analysis etc;
- Curriculum for a PhD in Translational Health Sciences. The curriculum was almost finalised during the inception phase and fully finalised in the next period.
- Curricula for 6 MSc Programs were developed: in Clinical Trials, Human Genetics and Genomics, Immunology, Infectious Diseases, Experimental Medicine (Animal Models), and Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics. The CT curriculum was almost finalised.
In addition, the MAV became more visible to stakeholders and a better coordination amongst them was developed. Trust between partners and stakeholder was being built.
The main output from the inception phase of the Vaccine uptake project was a comprehensive project proposal, which was received and assessed and resulted in agreements with the partners (intervention 16785). The project continues to be co-financed by Sida and IDRC.
The project convened several regional stakeholder meetings brought together policymakers, immunization managers, regulators, funders, vaccine manufacturers, and researchers from Rwanda, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, and Ethiopia. It resulted in stakeholder mapping, identification of research gaps and capacity needs, and the prioritization of research themes in social and behavioural sciences for vaccine uptake, and deepened regional collaboration and included international researchers from Sweden and Canada. It identified opportunities to strengthen locally led, contextually relevant research systems. The project conducted a scoping review on the roles, capacity needs, and opportunities for involving social and behavioural scientists in vaccine interventions in Eastern Africa. This review provided a foundational evidence base for future research and policy design.
Key outcomes include:
- A regional research agenda and stakeholder network
- Identification of critical capacity gaps and development priorities
- Strengthened institutional commitment and visibility
- A roadmap for scaling up behavioural research on vaccines in Eastern Africa
- A comprehensive grant proposal for a regional initiative on strengthening the capacity for social and behavioural science research on vaccine uptake informed by identified research and practice gaps.
While doing the mapping and holding the meetings, interest was identified in many areas in addition to vaccine uptake. This unexpected result further strengthens the commitment of the team to increase visibility and knowledge, to serve different areas in the future.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
